issues.title: Suspected oil-pressure loss with B235 knock: distinguish sensor, strainer and irreversible bearing damage
issues.cause: Factory bulletin distinguishes warning-lamp failure, intake restriction, chain noise, and lower-end bearing injury in MY98–03 B205/B235. No single symptom proves one cause.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Confirm actual oil pressure with approved gauge/test conditions, assess pattern of noise; pursue strainer and bearing inspection if bulletin conditions dictate before undertaking a PCV-only fix.
issues.correction_summary: Treat demonstrated bearing damage as engine/short-block scope, not as cured by sump cleaning or fresh oil; follow source-specific factory bulletin.
limits: WIS 2005 pressure spec is independent and is NOT claimed as the MY1998–2003 bulletin's numeric acceptance test without confirmation.
A pre-purchase listening test cannot establish remaining bearing life or pickup cleanliness.
Do not run an engine with demonstrably unsafe oil pressure to complete cosmetic checks.

issues.title: Cold-start misfire with hot-normal running: differentiate B207 intake-valve sealing loss
issues.cause: SPNA advisory identifies premature intake valve face wear as a possible explanation for severe cold compression loss that improves once hot.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Perform overnight-cold compression AND leak-down testing in a shop, compare with hot values and assess other fuel/ignition causes; do not stop at warm cranking numbers.
issues.correction_summary: If intake-valve wear is demonstrated, follow full TAC/repair information for cylinder-head valve work; source mentions 55563529 but does not certify head interchange.
limits: 2007–08 applies specifically to B207R; 2009–11 advisory references B207, and B284 is excluded.
AERA broad MY2003–11 technical discussion is NOT the same population as the SPNA advisory.
Cold/hot psi examples in secondary reproductions are inconsistent and are not a go/no-go threshold here.
No statistical fault frequency or preventive replacement recommendation is implied.

issues.title: FA57 hard shifts plus coolant in ATF: transmission replacement risk
issues.cause: Saab TA440-0702 attributes coolant contamination to insufficient sealing at cooler nipples in specifically listed early FA57 9-3s.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Check year/body/VIN and campaign history, determine whether ATF is contaminated by a qualified shop and separate fluid level faults from coolant ingress. DO NOT perform the bulletin's open-flame sample heating test as a home check.
issues.correction_summary: Once contamination is confirmed in this TSB context, factory recommends replacement transmission and rework of cooler/couplings/lines plus TCM adaptation.
limits: FA57 advice includes body-specific MY2003–05 VIN boundaries and is broader than the separate older CSP15446 campaign.
A poor shift or ATF level error alone does not prove coolant in the transmission.
No broad application to AF40, manual transaxles, or all MY2005 cars.
